# <span id="aanchor17"></span> Quality Assignment Editor

## Configuring Assignments

The options available when configuring assignments vary slightly between gas and liquid, and between meters and locations. The New and Edit functions will open the appropriate detail screen based on the selected object. Meters will open to the detail corresponding to the meter’s fluid phase; locations open to a detail tailored for liquid tickets.

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Gas Meter Assignment">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Gas Meter Assignment Details</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Gas Meter Assignment">

The following options are available on the gas meter assignment details screen:

- **Assignment** - The meter object selector will be populated from the previous screen. The source object selector will only display gas sources for gas meters.

- **Duration** - Assignments are date-effective.

- **Apply GQ At** - The earliest meter flow data date/time to which the analysis should be applied.
  - **Effective Date/Time** - Applies to the flow data record whose effective date/time matches the source analysis record. This is typical for online chromatographs.
  - **Start of Current Day** - Applies the source record back to the first hour of the current day. "Current day" refers to the date of the analysis record being applied including consideration of the meter’s contract hour. If there are multiple analyses in a measurement day, the last one will be used.
  - **Start of Current Month** - Applies the source record back to the first hour of the current month. "Current month" refers to the date of the analysis record being applied including consideration of the meter’s contract day and hour. If there are multiple analyses in a contract month, the last one will be used.
  - **Start of Next Day** - Applies the source record to the first hour of the next day. "Next day" is relative to the date of the analysis record being applied including consideration of the meter’s contract hour. if there are multiple analyses in a measurement day, the last one will be used.
  - **Start of Next Month** - Applies the source record to the first hour of the next month. "Next month" is relative to the analysis record being applied including consideration of the meter’s contract day and hour. If there are multiple analyses in a measurement month, the last one will be used.

- **Apply Extended As** - Dictates how a full or extended analysis (potentially 200+ components) is totaled for application to a meter.

  This only applies to source analyses designated as full analyses in the source detail.

- **Saturation** - The water vapor saturation condition of the heating value that is to be applied.
  - **Meter Condition** - Choose the heating value that matches the meter’s current heating value saturation.
  - **Dry Condition** - Apply the source’s dry heating value and alter the meter’s condition to dry.
  - **Wet Condition** - Apply the source’s wet heating value and alter the meter’s condition to wet.
  - **As Delivered Condition** - Apply the source’s as-delivered heating value and alter the meter’s condition to as-delivered.

- **Recalc. Method** - The calculation methodology to be used on the meter.
  - **Volume** - Recalculates the meter’s volume and energy using the applied relative density, VCF, and heating value.
  - **VCF** - Recalculates the meter’s VCF using the applied relative density, leaving the volume unchanged. By default, the energy will not be recalculated.
  - **Vol, Set VCF = 1** - Recalculates the meter’s volume and energy using the applied relative density and heating value and resetting the VCF to 1.

- **Enable Assignment** - Enables the source apply to proceed. This option is enabled by default on new assignments. It is only disabled in specific circumstances.

- **Use Prior When Current is Missing or Inhibited** - Enables the application of a prior analysis when the analyses that should be available for a given meter date/time is missing or marked as inhibited.

- **Copy Liquid Content** - Enables the copy of the source’s liquid content values (GPMs) to the meter.

- **Copy ASD Heating Value** - Enables the copy of the source’s as delivered heating value to the meter.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 540;height: 397;" />

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Liquid Meter Assignment">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Liquid Meter Assignment Details</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Liquid Meter Assignment">

The following options are available on the liquid meter assignment detail screen:

- **Assignment** - The meter object selector will be populated from the previous screen. The source object selector will only display liquid sources for liquid meters. If a non-hydrocarbon meter is selected, the source object selector will only display non-hydrocarbon sources.

- **Duration** - Assignments are date-effective. All assignment options will be effective only for the meter data that occurs within the effective date span of the assignment.

- **Apply Sample At** - The flow data date/time to which the analysis should be applied.
  - **End of Batch** - Apply the sample, whose sample date is within tolerance of the batch end date, to entire batch. Tolerance is specified in the on the [Liquids &gt; Setup tab](../../Meters/Meter%20Editor/Liquids%20Tab.md) of the Meter Editor.
  - **Effective Date/Time** - Applies to the flow data record whose effective date/time matches the source analysis record. This is typical for online chromatographs.

- **Apply Extended As**\* - Dictates how a full or extended analysis (potentially 200+ components) is totaled for application to a meter.

  This only applies to source analyses designated as full analyses in the source detail.

- **Apply Density**\* - Signifies if the meter quantities will be recalculated using the source density. In all cases, the analysis information will be copied to the meter and used to calculate component masses, component volumes, and summed volume.
  - **Do Not Apply** - The flow data quantities gross standard volume, net standard volume and total mass will not be altered when the analysis is copied to the meter. Only the component quantities and summed volume are calculated.
  - **Base Relative Density** - The source’s base relative density will be copied to the meter’s observed density and the meter’s observed temperature will be set to the product base temperature and the observed pressure will be set to 0 gauge pressure or the product EVP. Calculation of the flow data quantities will be initiated.
  - **Base API Gravity** - The source’s base API gravity will be copied to the meter’s observed density and the meter’s observed temperature will be set to the product base temperature and the observed pressure will be set to 0 gauge pressure or the product EVP. Calculation of the flow data quantities will be initiated.
  - **Base Density (in vac.)** - The source’s base absolute density in vacuo will be converted to meter density units and copied to the meter’s observed density, the meter’s observed temperature will be set to the product base temperature and the observed pressure will be set to 0 gauge pressure or the product EVP. Calculation of the flow data quantities will be initiated.
  - **Sample Relative Density** - The source’s sample relative density, sample temperature, and sample pressure will be copied to the meter’s observed density, observed temperature, and observed pressure, respectively. Calculation of the flow data quantities will be initiated.
  - **Sample API Gravity** - The source’s sample API gravity, sample temperature, and sample pressure will be copied to the meter’s observed density, observed temperature, and observed pressure, respectively. Calculation of the flow data quantities will be initiated.
  - **Sample Density (in vac.)** - The source’s sample absolute density in vacuo, sample temperature, and sample pressure will be copied to the meter’s observed density, observed temperature, and observed pressure, respectively. Calculation of the flow data quantities will be initiated.

- **Recalc. Method** - The calculation methodology to be used on the meter.
  - **Vol. and Mass, Use CF** - Recalculates the meter’s gross standard volume, net standard volume and mass using the applied density and VCF. This is the most common method.
  - **Correlation Factor (CF)** - Recalculates the meter’s correlation factors using the applied density, leaving the volume and mass quantities unchanged.
  - **Vol. and Mass, Set CF = 1** - Recalculates the meter’s volume and mass quantities using the applied density and resetting the correlation factors to 1.

- **Enable Assignment** - Enables the source apply to proceed. This option is enabled by default on new assignments. It is only disabled in specific circumstances.

- **Use Prior When Current is Missing or Inhibited** - Enables the application of a prior analysis when the analyses that should be available for a given meter date/time is missing or marked as inhibited.

- **Apply Back to Prior Sample** - Enables the application of a sample to multiple batches beginning from the prior sample’s effective date. This is useful when samples are not retrieved for every batch, such as daily batches.

- **Apply Back Within Sample Month Only** - Limits the prior sample application to the current month. This can prevent PPAs from being created.

  This option can only be enabled when **Apply Back to Prior Sample** option is enabled.

- **Use First Sample** - Enables use of the first sample, by chronological sample date, on an End of Batch assignment with [sample tolerance](../../Meters/Meter%20Editor/Liquids%20Tab.md) set. By default, the last sample is used when there are multiple samples within the sample tolerance.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 542;height: 396;" />

\*Options are disabled for non-hydrocarbon meters.

**See also:** [Liquid Meter Assignment - Options Details](Liquid%20Meter%20Assignment%20Ops%20Dets.md)

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Location Assignment">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Location Assignment Details</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Location Assignment">

The following options are available on the location assignment detail screen:

- **Assignment** - The location object selector will be populated from the previous screen. The source object selector will only display liquid sources.

- **Duration** - Assignments are date-effective.

- **Apply Sample At** - The date/time to which the analysis should be applied.
  - **Effective Date/Time** - Applies the analysis to tickets whose effective date/time matches the sample date/time. When used in conjunction with the **Use Prior…** option, all future tickets will use the same analysis until a new sample is received.
  - **Start of Current Day** - The analysis date/time is adjusted to the start of the day (contract hour) and applied to tickets whose effective date/time matches the adjusted sample date/time. When used in conjunction with the **Use Prior…** option, all tickets in the current day and those in the future will use the same analysis until a new sample is received.
  - **Start of Current Month** - The analysis date/time is adjusted to the start of the current month (contract day, contract hour) and applied to tickets whose effective date/time matches the adjusted sample date/time. When used in conjunction with the **Use Prior…** option, all tickets in the current month and those in the future will use the same analysis until a new sample is received.

- **Apply Extended As** - Dictates how a full or extended analysis (potentially 200+ components) is totaled for application to a ticket.

  This only applies to source analyses designated as full analyses in the source detail.

- **Apply Density** - Signifies if the ticket quantities will be recalculated using the source density. In all cases, the analysis information will be copied to the ticket and used to calculate component masses, component volumes, and summed volume.
  - **Do Not Apply** - The flow data quantities gross standard volume, net standard volume, and total mass will not be altered when the analysis is copied to the ticket. Only the component quantities and summed volume are calculated.
  - **Base Relative Density** - The source’s base relative density will be copied to the ticket’s observed density and the ticket’s observed temperature and pressure will be set to base temperature and base pressure, respectively. Calculation of the flow data quantities will be initiated.
  - **Base API Gravity** - The source’s base API gravity will be copied to the ticket’s observed density and the ticket’s observed temperature and pressure will be set to base temperature and base pressure, respectively. Calculation of the flow data quantities will be initiated.
  - **Base Density (in vac.)** - The source’s base absolute density in vacuo will be converted to ticket density units and copied to the ticket’s observed density, and the ticket’s observed temperature and pressure will be set to base temperature and base pressure, respectively. Calculation of the flow data quantities will be initiated.
  - **Sample Relative Density** - The source’s sample relative density, sample temperature, and sample pressure will be copied to the ticket’s observed density, observed temperature, and observed pressure, respectively. Calculation of the flow data quantities will be initiated.
  - **Sample API Gravity** - The source’s sample API gravity, sample temperature, and sample pressure will be copied to the ticket’s observed density, observed temperature, and observed pressure, respectively. Calculation of the flow data quantities will be initiated.
  - **Sample Density (in vac.)** - The source’s sample absolute density in vacuo, sample temperature, and sample pressure will be copied to the ticket’s observed density, observed temperature, and observed pressure, respectively. Calculation of the flow data quantities will be initiated.

- **Recalc. Method** - The calculation methodology to be used on the ticket.
  - **Vol. and Mass, Use CF** - Recalculates the ticket’s gross standard volume, net standard volume, and mass using the applied density and VCF. This is the most common method.
  - **Correlation Factor (CF)** - Recalculates the ticket’s correlation factors using the applied density, leaving the volume and mass quantities unchanged.
  - **Vol. and Mass, Set CF = 1** - Recalculates the ticket’s volume and mass quantities using the applied density and resetting the correlation factors to 1.

- **Enable Assignment** - Enables the source apply to proceed. This option is enabled by default on new assignments. It is only disabled in specific circumstances.

- **Use Prior When Current is Missing or Inhibited** - Enables the application of a prior analysis when the analyses that should be available for a given ticket date/time is missing or marked as inhibited.
